intelligence.essence: Dependency-Ordered Invariant Proof Law: NayaNET shall define machine-checkable dependencies among observation, temporal, lifecycle, authority, budget, resource, cycle-preservation and exit invariants. Verification shall establish prerequisites before conclusions, distinguish false from unresolved evidence, and identify the earliest reachable causal failure rather than the first arbitrarily evaluated check. Counterexamples shall be minimized only while preserving the original authoritative model, valid transitions, necessary constraints and independent replay evidence. The behavior: 'I found that this cycle cannot repeat. I know exactly which condition fails first, which other failures result from it, and the shortest valid sequence that proves it. I can reproduce that conclusion independently without removing the constraints that made the failure possible.'
intelligence.falsifier: Authority failure reported when the root cause is a missing policy record; a cycle declared repeatable after silently ignoring budget/terminal constraints; a minimized counterexample that is no longer executable under the actual model; UNDETERMINED promoted to PROVEN_FALSE; solver timeout/UNKNOWN treated as proof of no counterexample; unreachable-state solver artifacts presented as executable counterexamples; dependency cycles broken by arbitrary check ordering instead of joint verification; minimized witnesses that drop expiry constraints passing the checker.

human_view.meaning: Checking things in the right order and blaming the right thing are different skills — the system needs both. Six invariant families with explicit dependencies: observations first (are the records real?), then time and versions, then whether the obligation is still alive, then authority, then budgets and resources, then the cycle itself, then the exit. But when something fails, the report follows causality, not the checklist: if LAW expired because time ran out, the diagnosis says 'temporal authorization expiry' with 'authority invalid' as the downstream consequence — not just 'authority=false'. The authority-expires-after-one-cycle example shows the ideal output: primary failure named, dependent failure distinguished, budget explicitly cleared, minimal trace given. Three-valued logic throughout: proven true, proven false, or undetermined — and undetermined never becomes false. The F1/F6 pairing is the epistemic honesty test: with complete evidence of expiry, produce the minimal one-cycle counterexample; with missing time evidence, preserve UNDETERMINED and trigger reconstruction instead of fabricating the same counterexample. Counterexamples get minimized lexicographically — earliest failing boundary, fewest transitions, fewest predicates, smallest evidence set — but the reduced trace must remain executable under the original model, with the original witness preserved alongside. Dependency cycles (budget needs resource needs budget) get joint verification, not arbitrary ordering. Twelve fixtures covering expiry, exhaustion, resource loss, terminal transitions, policy changes, missing records, simultaneous independent failures, joint-dependency cycles, unreachable artifacts, strategy-specific failure, minimization that drops constraints, and the fully valid case.

intelligence.learning_lesson: This is the diagnostic layer over AER-LIVE-8's invariants: AER-LIVE-8 defined what to prove; AER-LIVE-9 defines how to check it, blame failures, and explain them. Permanent contributions: the dependency-order vs causal-order vs execution-order trichotomy (proof construction follows dependencies; failure reports follow causality); the 7-stage default verification order (observation → temporal/version → lifecycle → authority → budget/resource → cycle → exit) with the parallel-budget/resource note; the invariant dependency contract schema (requires/provides/predicate_ref/evidence_refs/preservation_target/on_false/on_unknown) with the three semantic outcomes and the UNDETERMINED-≠-FALSE rule; the five proof obligations (entry, enabledness, preservation, debt gain, exit) with the reachable-counterexample requirement (solver artifacts in unreachable states don't count); the existential-vs-universal reasoning discipline with the four verdicts (WITNESS_INVALID / UNBOUNDEDNESS_NOT_ESTABLISHED / FINITE_UPPER_BOUND_PROVEN / UNBOUNDED_IN_MODEL); the causal first-failure protocol (earliest reachable boundary, all failures there, root-vs-dependent separation, no invented ordering, trace minimization preserving order); the authority-expiry worked example as the diagnostic ideal; the lexicographic counterexample minimization (boundary → transitions → predicates → evidence) with the Reachable∧ValidTransitions∧FailureReproduced preservation and the local-vs-global minimality honesty; the dependency-cycle joint-verification rule (I_joint with complete-transition preservation; unresolved cycles are proof gaps, not deadlock proofs); the verifier pseudocode with the FALSE-needs-counterexample / UNKNOWN-stays-unresolved / timeout-≠-proof requirements; the AER-LIVE-9 failure receipt schema with original-witness retention; and the F1–F12 suite with the F1-vs-F6 expiry-proven vs expiry-unknown pairing as the honesty gate. Shawn's scoping stands: not established as implemented; separate from production promotion. Queued for the next build wave.

naya_view.directive: Verify in dependency order; diagnose in causal order. Establish prerequisites before conclusions; keep false and unresolved strictly separate. Find the earliest reachable failure boundary; separate root causes from consequences; report simultaneous independent failures without inventing order. Minimize counterexamples lexicographically while preserving executability under the original model. Verify dependency cycles jointly. Never promote timeouts to proofs. Prove F1–F12 with the F1-vs-F6 honesty pair as the gate.
